chunks: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Hakim ibn Hukaym who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgets a rak'ah or a sajdah or something of it in his prayer, then remembers afterwards, so he said: 'He completes that specific one.' I said: 'Does he repeat the prayer?' He said: 'No.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: If he doubts while standing whether it is the ruku', he performs ruku', and if he has already entered another state such as sajdah or other, he proceeds in his prayer and there is nothing upon him. And this is also if it is in the last two rak'ahs, because if it is in the first two rak'ahs, it is obligatory upon him to restart the prayer because he has not completed their number and he is doubting in them. And it has been said that every forgetfulness that befalls a person in the first two, he must repeat the prayer. And that which indicates the first division from what we presented earlier is what he narrated:

key_terms.رَكْعَة: A unit of prayer consisting of standing, bowing, and prostrating

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets a rak'ah during the last two units of prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *sahw* (inadvertent error) in the first two versus the last two rak'ahs, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding whether the prayer is invalidated or merely completed. Shaykh al-Tusi notes the scholarly debate, highlighting that while some argue any error in the first two rak'ahs necessitates a full restart (*isti'naf*), the preferred view aligns with the Prophet's instruction to simply compensate for the specific missed element. This ruling emphasizes the principle of ease (*yusr*) in worship, ensuring that minor forgetfulness does not nullify the entire act of devotion.
